method: Read the run fn of every spec in crates/engine/src/cmd/*.rs (16 spec files) plus lib.rs, recovery.rs and guard.rs, and rg'd the engine for std::fs, env, UiRequest pushes, nested s.execute calls and clipboard use; for the UiRequest stubs (media.play/pause/toggle/stop/seek, show.fromStart/fromCurrent, the PickFile fallback of file.save*) I read what the egui host does with them in crates/ui-egui. Verified: every nested execute uses a fixed inner id (no caller-chosen command ever runs, so nothing is `code`), the clipboard is the engine's own Session.clipboard (the OS clipboard's text only arrives as edit.paste's `text` param), and the pptx/format importers record external link targets as strings without reading files or URLs. Not counted per command: guard.rs writes AutoRecover files for every open document when any command panics and the host set recovery_dir, and text layout lazily scans the OS font folders (deckcraft-fonts FontDb::load_system_fonts), both host-controlled and never caller-chosen. Classes are for the pinned revision d0e57d7; a headless session (OctoSense deck host-service) has recovery_dir unset and nobody draining ui_requests, so the device rules and the PickFile branch are stubs there.

rules.why: file.open reads `path` with std::fs::read and opens it as a deck; file.export renders PNG/JPEG per slide (multiple slides become `<stem>N.<ext>` siblings), PDF, PPTX, outline or native bytes and writes each to `path` through write_file (std::fs::write to `<path>.saving`, then std::fs::rename).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:226-273 export(): write_file per output (png/jpeg loop, pdf, save_bytes formats)

rules.why: AutoRecover in the host-set Session.recovery_dir (default ~/Library/Application Support/DeckCraft/Recovery, %APPDATA%\DeckCraft\Recovery or $XDG_DATA_HOME/deckcraft/recovery): save create_dir_all's it and writes `<uid>.deckcraft` + `<uid>.json`; list read_dir's it and reads each JSON; open std::fs::read's every entry into a new document (taking its stored `path`) and deletes the entry; discard remove_file's one or all entries.
evidence: crates/engine/src/recovery.rs:52-70 save(): create_dir_all, std::fs::write + rename, meta JSON
crates/engine/src/recovery.rs:73-113 list(): read_dir/read_to_string; open(): std::fs::read, DocState with recovered path

rules.why: Naming trap: these file.* ids never touch a path. file.new builds a deck from a built-in theme, file.openBytes decodes base64 `data` (pptx external links stay strings), file.saveBytes returns the encoded deck as base64, file.render returns a slide PNG as base64, file.properties edits doc.props, and file.revert restores the in-memory saved snapshot (DocState.saved_doc) without re-reading the file.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:282-313 properties()/revert(): s.edit on doc.props; st.doc = st.saved_doc
crates/pptx/src/opc.rs:106-108 external relationship targets kept as strings

rules.why: With `path`, or the document's stored DocState.path (which file.open, file.saveAs and file.recovery.open set), they encode the deck and write it through write_file like file.export. With neither they only return needsPath and queue UiRequest::PickFile, which the egui host turns into a native Save dialog (services.pick_save) before calling file.saveAs (a stub when headless). host is stricter than file. A door that always passes a caller-folder `path` could treat them as file, but must remember that a missing `path` falls back to the stored path.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:182-201 save()/save_as(): path param or d.path, else UiRequest::PickFile
crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:156-168 mark_saved(): also recovery::discard of the entry

rules.why: Closes the active document in memory, but Session::close_document then calls recovery::discard, which std::fs::remove_file's that document's `<uid>.deckcraft`/`<uid>.json` AutoRecover entry whenever the host set recovery_dir (None headless, where it touches nothing).
evidence: crates/engine/src/lib.rs:373-381 close_document(): recovery::discard(dir, d.uid) when recovery_dir is set

rules.why: Naming trap: window.next only changes which open document of the session is active (Session::set_active); no OS window or panel is involved.

Undo/redo swap Arc snapshots of the deck; cut/copy/paste use the engine's own Session.clipboard (edit.copy returns the text for the host to place on the OS clipboard, and edit.paste/pasteText take the OS clipboard's text as the caller's `text` param); duplicate/delete/select edit the deck. Nested calls are fixed ids (insert.textBox, slide.delete, text.selectAll).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:158-245 paste()/paste_text(): `text` param or s.clipboard; fixed insert.textBox

rules.why: Slide list, layout, notes, hide, rename, editor navigation (slide.go/next/previous/first/last move Selection.slide, not a slideshow) and slide selection edit the open deck; slide.fromOutline parses its `text` param; slide.inspect returns JSON.
Add, rename, remove and move sections in doc.sections of the open deck.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs:37-49 section.* specs; 488-571 section_add..section_move: s.edit on doc.sections

rules.why: Geometry, outline, effects, quick styles, names, alt text, visibility, lock, connectors and freeforms (fixed shape.insert), shape.merge boolean ops, the preset gallery, connection sites and shape.inspect JSON all act on the deck; shape.setDefault keeps the look in Session.default_look.

Naming trap: the params advertise `picture?: base64`, but both pass `picture` to insert::media_bytes as `data` via with_param, which keeps every other caller key. A non-string `picture` (e.g. null) leaves `data` unreadable, so media_bytes falls through to an undocumented `path` and std::fs::read's that file into the deck as a picture fill or background.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/shape.rs:276-280 fill(): p.get(picture).is_some() -> media_bytes(&with_param(p, data, picture))
crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:186-190 with_param(): clones all params, inserts `data`

rules.why: Text boxes, tables, charts, WordArt, SmartArt (fixed arrange.group + shape.rename), symbols, action buttons and slide-number/date fields (fixed design.headerFooter) edit the deck. insert.hyperlink only stores the URL or slide target as a click action (Action::Url); nothing in the engine fetches it.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs:570-589 hyperlink(): Action::Url { url } stored on the run or shape

rules.why: Besides base64 `data`, all four accept `path`, and insert::media_bytes std::fs::read's it (any file the process can read) and embeds the bytes in the deck. insert.audio/video also queue an unplayable-codec warning as a UiRequest::Message status line, which I did not count as host.
Change chart type, data and elements on a chart shape in the deck.
Crop, corrections and reset edit the picture fill of shapes in the deck.

media.play/pause/toggle/stop/seek only push UiRequest::Media for the UI host (a stub when headless, since nothing drains ui_requests); the egui host plays the clip through deckcraft-media's Player with the cpal audio output and video feeds.
evidence: crates/ui-egui/src/media.rs:1-2,51 MediaHost: Player (audio out + clocks), cpal AudioOut injected

rules.why: media.options sets playback fields on the MediaClip in the deck; media.info probes the embedded media bytes and returns the host-reported Session.media_status; media.posterFrame decodes a frame of the embedded video in memory and stores it as the poster.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/media.rs:132-149 poster_frame(): poster_png from embedded bytes

rules.why: Z-order, group/ungroup/regroup, align, distribute, rotate, flip and nudge on the deck (rotate/flip/nudge delegate to fixed shape.rotate/flip/move).
In-place text editing, caret and selection, set/get text on shapes, table cells and notes (smart quotes and autocorrect read Session.prefs).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:14 specs(): text.* run fns use s.edit / s.select only (no fs, no ui_requests)

rules.why: Character and paragraph formatting on the selection (font is a family name stored in the run); the Format Painter keeps its copied formatting in Session.painter; format.state is a query.
Themes, colour and font schemes come from built-ins (or names/hex values in params); slide size, header/footer and hide-background-graphics edit the deck.
view.slideMaster/closeMaster switch Selection.target, i.e. which shape tree (slides, a master or a layout) later commands edit; engine editing state, not a UI-only view.
Insert, rename and delete layouts and insert placeholders in the deck's slide masters.
Set, time, apply-to-all and list slide transitions stored in the deck.
Add, remove, reorder, time and list shape animations stored on the slides.
Rows, columns, merges, styles, shading, sizes and cell selection on table shapes in the deck.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:9 specs(): edit_shapes / s.select on ShapeKind::Table

rules.why: Comments and replies stored on the slides (author from Session.prefs, date from the system clock).
Read-only checks of the deck: missing titles/alt text and contrast, and spelling against a small built-in word list (no dictionary files).

show.fromStart/fromCurrent only push UiRequest::StartShow (a stub when headless). The egui host then starts the slide show full screen (ViewportCommand::Fullscreen), opens the presenter window when presenter view is on, and autoplays slide media through the audio output.
Store slide-show settings (doc.show) and named custom shows (doc.custom_shows) in the deck; nothing starts.
document.inspect returns the deck summary as JSON (its stored path is reported, never opened).
commands.list returns the registry (Session::commands) filtered by a substring; it runs nothing.
